name: A mypy error: which fix?
shape_md: Sample Q3. One `mypy --strict` error under a few lines of code, and four fixes. Expect one of these on the paper, with a different error.
one_md: Read the bracket at the end of the error, name the kind, and pick the fix that removes the cause.

sample.question_md:
`mypy --strict` reports this error on the code below:

```python
def find_expense(expenses: list[Expense], expense_id: int) -> Expense | None: ...

expense = find_expense(expenses, 3)
total += expense.amount
```

```text
error: Item "None" of "Expense | None" has no attribute "amount"  [union-attr]
```

Which fix is most appropriate?
options: Add `# type: ignore` to the line
Change the return type of `find_expense` to `Any`
Delete the type annotations from the function
sample.his_answer_md: **b.** The error says the value can be None. Handle that case. `# type: ignore` and `Any` hide the problem and keep the crash. Removing annotations makes the checker blind.
sample.decoded_md:
- The pattern: one error line, one fix to pick. The bracket `[union-attr]` says "this can be missing".
- b is right because it removes the cause. After a `None` check the crash cannot happen.
- a, c and d are the careless moves. They silence mypy, give up on the value, or switch the checker off. The crash stays.
- His reason is three short sentences: what the error says, what to do, why the others fail. That is the length to aim for.

spot_md:
- One `error:` line from `mypy --strict`, with a code in square brackets.
- Four fixes, and two of them are `# type: ignore` or `Any`.
- The question says "most appropriate" or "which fix".
- On a different topic: the same error on a `dict.get`, a search that finds nothing, or an optional argument.

basics.heading: Four kinds of mypy error, four honest fixes
basics.body_md:
mypy reports one line per problem. The code in square brackets tells you the kind, and the kind tells you the fix.

| What mypy says | Kind | Honest fix |
|---|---|---|
| `Function is missing a type annotation` | missing annotation | write the types in the signature |
| `Item "None" of ... has no attribute` | None not handled | check for `None` before using the value |
| `Incompatible types in assignment` | types disagree | make both sides the same type, such as `0.0` for a float |
| `Returning Any from function declared to return "float"` | Any leaks in | give the value a real type, such as `float(...)` |

The careless moves are the same every time. `# type: ignore` hides the line. `Any` says you gave up on the value. Deleting annotations switches the checker off. None of them removes the crash, so none of them is the fix.

checks.q_md: mypy says `Item "None" of "Expense | None" has no attribute "amount"`. What can happen when the program runs?
options: Nothing: it is only a style warning
An `AttributeError` when no expense is found
The program prints the wrong amount
checks.why_md: If `find_expense` returns `None`, asking it for `.amount` raises `AttributeError`.

checks.q_md: Which of these removes the cause of the error?
options: An `if expense is None` check before the line
checks.why_md: Only the check makes the crash impossible. The other two keep it and hide it.

method: Read the error line and the bracket at the end. Say the kind in your own words.
Ask what could go wrong when the program runs: a `None`, a wrong type, a missing hint.
Reject the careless options: `# type: ignore`, `Any`, deleting annotations, upgrading.
Pick the option that removes the cause, and say why in one sentence.

worked.title: The same shape on another topic
worked.question_md:
`mypy --strict` reports this error:

```python
total = 0
for expense in expenses:
    total += expense.amount
```

```text
error: Incompatible types in assignment (expression has type "float", variable has type "int")  [assignment]
```

Which fix is most appropriate?

- a) Add `# type: ignore`
- b) Start the total at `0.0`
- c) Declare `total: Any`
- d) Remove the type hints from the file
steps_md: The bracket says `assignment`: the variable was an `int` and now receives a `float`.
a, c and d silence or switch off the check. The types still disagree.
b makes the variable a `float` from the start.
worked.answer_md: **b.** The amounts are floats, so `0.0` makes both sides agree. The other options hide the mismatch.

twists.twist_md: The error is `Missing positional argument` or `Function is missing a type annotation`.
twists.how_md: Name the kind first. A missing annotation is fixed in the signature, not with `# type: ignore`.

twists.twist_md: The return type of `find_expense` is `Expense`, and the fix offered is `if expense is None`.
twists.how_md: That check is dead code. Say the declared type already promises a value.

twists.twist_md: One option is `Optional[Expense]` on the caller's variable.
twists.how_md: It declares the problem instead of handling it. The crash stays.

traps: `# type: ignore` is tempting because CI goes green. The crash stays, and now nobody sees it.
`Any` feels like a fix. It means mypy stops checking that value.
Deleting the annotations makes the error disappear and the checker blind.
say_md:
- the error says the value can be `None`, so handle that case
- `# type: ignore` and `Any` hide the problem and keep the crash
- name the kind: missing annotation, None not handled, types disagree, Any leaks in
